names_aka: cathodic arc evaporation / cathodic arc deposition
gold-color PVD stack (nitride base + Au top flash)
principle: Source material is converted to vapor in vacuum — by resistive heating of a boat/filament (thermal evaporation), by a focused electron beam melting a crucible pool (e-beam), or by a low-voltage high-current arc whose cathode spots explosively erode the target into a highly ionized metal plasma (cathodic arc, ionized fraction ~30-100% vs <1% for evaporation) — and condenses line-of-sight on the substrate. 'Ion plating' adds a negative substrate bias in a plasma so the growing film is continuously bombarded by energetic ions: this sputter-cleans the interface, drives shallow ion mixing, and densifies the film, giving the adhesion and density that plain evaporation lacks (Mattox concept, standard PVD-handbook material). With N2 as reactive gas, arc-evaporated Ti forms TiN — golden-colored, ~2000-2400 HV ceramic — which is the basis of the watch/jewelry industry's scratch-resistant gold look: 0.5-3 um TiN (or paler ZrN) base + 0.05-0.3 um real gold/gold-alloy top flash for true karat color; the soft Au cap wears into the hard nitride which keeps the color. Where these beat sputtering: evaporation beats it on deposition rate, hardware simplicity and low working-gas incorporation for pure soft Au flash coats; cathodic arc beats it on ionization fraction (hence adhesion, film density, hardness) and on rate for thick hard nitrides — its penalty is emitted molten macroparticles ('droplets') unless magnetically filtered. [FACT: published typical PVD-handbook description]

substrates: stainless steel (best anchor for decorative PVD: no pore-corrosion of substrate, takes 200-450 C)
hardened/spring steels (ONLY if deposition temperature stays below tempering temperature)
brass and Zn diecast (need Ni or Cr electroplated leveling/barrier layer first; Zn outgasses — low-temp process required)
glass, ceramic, some plastics (PVD needs NO electrical conductivity — this is the route for glass houseware; plastics need low-temp evaporation + lacquer, not hot arc)
applicability.steel_wire_notes: PVD is line-of-sight and batch: wire/rings must be racked on 2-3-axis rotating (planetary) fixtures to coat all around; a continuous vacuum feed-through wire line (owner's Q1 concept) is industrially exotic for arc/evaporation and needs differential-pumped slit seals — realistic answer: FORM the steel wire into rings first, then batch-coat the finished rings. Critical ordering constraint: nitride PVD stacks CANNOT be formed after coating (ceramic film cracks at <~1-2% strain) and arc deposition at 200-450 C can draw the temper of spring steel — coat last, on stainless or on already-hardened-and-tempered parts, or specify a low-temperature (<200 C) arc/sputter hybrid process. PVD films are thin and not pore-free: on plain carbon steel, pinholes rust; use stainless wire (304/316) or an electroplated Ni barrier under the PVD stack. [FACT: standard decorative-PVD practice]
applicability.non_conductive_notes: Glass cups, ceramic: directly coatable by evaporation or arc PVD (no seed layer needed, unlike electroplating) — adhesion on glass usually via 5-20 nm Cr/NiCr or Ti adhesion layer under Au; bare evaporated Au on glass wipes off. Food-contact status of TiN/Au PVD on drinkware rim/interior: [UNKNOWN — needs food-contact regulation check per market]; exterior-decorative only is the safe default.
applicability.jewelry_thickness_classes: All PVD gold layers are FLASH class by electroplating vocabulary: evaporated/sputtered/arc Au top coat 0.05-0.3 um typical; the wear thickness is carried by the 0.5-3 um nitride, not by gold. A plain evaporated-Au-only finish (no nitride, no lacquer) is a promotional/costume flash that wears in weeks. Micron-gold classes (ASTM B488 / ISO 27874 electrodeposit thickness classes) are NOT reachable economically by PVD — that is electroplating territory. [FACT: published typical practice]

components.name: vacuum chamber
components.purpose: stainless bell jar or box chamber, 50-1000 L class for jewelry batch coaters; holds base pressure 1e-3 to 1e-4 Pa
components.diy_notes: DIY thermal evaporation: glass bell jar or welded SS pot, ISO-KF/CF ports; implosion shielding mandatory for glass

components.name: pumping stack
components.purpose: rotary vane or scroll roughing pump + turbomolecular or oil-diffusion high-vacuum pump; base <5e-3 Pa before deposition
components.diy_notes: used 2-stage rotary + small diffusion pump is the classic cheap DIY stack; turbo is cleaner but costlier

components.name: pressure gauges
components.purpose: Pirani (rough) + ionization or capacitance gauge (high vacuum); process pressure control for reactive gas
components.diy_notes: a Pirani alone cannot read below ~1e-1 Pa reliably — DIY builds routinely fail here by never knowing true base pressure

components.name: evaporation source (thermal)
components.purpose: W or Mo boat/basket/coil resistively heated by low-voltage (5-15 V) high-current (50-300 A) transformer; holds the Au charge
components.diy_notes: most DIY-accessible PVD source; microwave-oven-transformer-class rewinds are commonly used (electrically hazardous — treat as mains-lethal)

components.name: e-beam gun (optional)
components.purpose: 270-degree-deflected electron beam melts source in water-cooled Cu crucible; for refractory adhesion layers (Ti, Cr) and high rates
components.diy_notes: HV (6-10 kV) + X-ray and interlock requirements put this beyond sensible DIY

components.name: cathodic arc source(s)
components.purpose: water-cooled Ti/Zr target with arc igniter and steering/confinement magnets; 60-100 A class DC arc supply per source; produces the ionized metal plasma for TiN/ZrN
components.diy_notes: NOT DIY-feasible: arc power supplies, cooling, droplet management and process control are industrial-grade; buy used coater or use a toll-coating job shop

components.name: substrate bias supply
components.purpose: DC or pulsed-DC negative bias, ~ -50 to -1000 V, applied to rotating fixture: ion etch at high bias, film densification at low bias (the defining element of ion plating)
components.diy_notes: a simple HV DC supply + isolated rotating contact; feasible for hobby glow-discharge cleaning

components.name: gas manifold with MFCs
components.purpose: Ar (etch/working gas) and N2 (reactive gas) via mass-flow controllers; N2 flow sets nitride stoichiometry and therefore COLOR
components.diy_notes: needle valves work for Ar; color-stable TiN realistically needs closed-loop flow/pressure control

components.name: substrate heater + thermocouple
components.purpose: preheat/outgas parts, hold 200-450 C during arc TiN for adhesion and stoichiometry
components.diy_notes: quartz lamp or resistive heater; cheap

components.name: rotating planetary fixture
components.purpose: 2-3-axis rotation so line-of-sight flux wraps around rings/wire pieces; also carries the bias
components.diy_notes: rotary vacuum feedthrough + gear train; a known DIY pain point (grease outgassing)

components.name: quartz crystal microbalance (QCM)
components.purpose: live thickness/rate monitor for evaporated layers (nm-resolution)
components.diy_notes: cheap used monitors exist; for arc nitrides thickness is instead set by time at calibrated rate

components.name: shutter
components.purpose: blocks source until rate is stable and pre-melt spatter is over; defines layer start/stop

operation_sequence.action: wet-clean parts offline (ultrasonic alkaline degrease, rinse, DI rinse, solvent/IPA dry or vapor degrease) and rack on planetary fixture with clean gloves
operation_sequence.parameters: cleanliness to water-break-free; no fingerprints (Na/Cl kill adhesion)
operation_sequence.failure_watch: any residual oil = guaranteed delamination; PVD is less forgiving than electroplating pretreatment

operation_sequence.action: load chamber, rough-pump then high-vacuum pump to base pressure
operation_sequence.parameters: base <= 5e-3 Pa (decorative) to 5e-4 Pa (quality work) [FACT: published typical range]
operation_sequence.failure_watch: stalling pressure = leak or wet/oily parts; do not start deposition, films will be brown/hazy

operation_sequence.parameters: 150-450 C per substrate limit; spring steel: stay below its tempering temperature [FACT: metallurgy]
operation_sequence.failure_watch: Zn diecast and plastics outgas violently; temper loss softens spring-steel rings

operation_sequence.action: plasma etch: Ar glow discharge or Ti arc-ion etch at high negative bias to sputter-clean surfaces
operation_sequence.parameters: Ar 0.5-5 Pa glow at -500 to -1500 V (glow) or arc-ion etch at -600 to -1000 V bias, minutes-class [ESTIMATE: handbook-range, high confidence]
operation_sequence.failure_watch: skipping/shortening this is the no.1 adhesion failure cause; overdoing arc etch overheats thin wire pieces

operation_sequence.action: deposit metallic adhesion interlayer: Ti (arc route) or Cr/NiCr 5-50 nm (evaporation route)
operation_sequence.parameters: arc: 60-100 A per source, bias -50 to -200 V, 1-3 min; evap: 0.1-0.5 nm/s by QCM [ESTIMATE: handbook-range, high confidence]
operation_sequence.failure_watch: no interlayer on steel/glass = peeling Au; Cr boat evaporation spits

operation_sequence.action: reactive step: admit N2 and grow TiN (or ZrN) hard color base
operation_sequence.parameters: total pressure ~0.5-4 Pa, N2 flow closed-loop to color setpoint; arc 60-100 A/source; bias -50 to -300 V; substrate 200-450 C; rate ~1-3 um/h; target 0.5-3 um [FACT: published typical arc-TiN window]
operation_sequence.failure_watch: N2 too low = grey/metallic sub-stoichiometric film; too high = brownish over-stoichiometric + target poisoning; droplets/spits = pinholes

operation_sequence.action: gold top flash: evaporate or sputter or arc-deposit Au / Au-alloy cap for true gold color
operation_sequence.parameters: 0.05-0.3 um; evap rate 0.1-1 nm/s by QCM; alloying (e.g. Au-Cu) shifts toward red/rose tones per ISO 8654 color classes [FACT: ISO 8654 gold-color designation system exists]
operation_sequence.failure_watch: too-thin cap = nitride tint shows through; contaminated Au charge = dull color

operation_sequence.action: cool under vacuum below ~100 C before venting
operation_sequence.parameters: vent with dry N2, not room air, to limit staining
operation_sequence.failure_watch: hot venting oxidizes/stains and can pop coatings via thermal shock

operation_sequence.action: unload, inspect color against master plates, run acceptance tests on samples
operation_sequence.failure_watch: check sharp edges and shadowed inner surfaces of rings — thinnest points

operation_sequence.action: periodic chamber maintenance: strip shields, clean flaked deposit, replace boats/targets
operation_sequence.parameters: wet-wipe Ti-dust (fine Ti dust is flammable) [FACT: hazard]
operation_sequence.failure_watch: flaking shield debris causes particle defects in following batches

prep_chain_required: 1. mechanical finish to final gloss BEFORE coating — PVD replicates every scratch; polish/tumble rings to mirror or desired texture first (WHY: 1-3 um conformal film hides nothing)
2. ultrasonic alkaline degrease + rinse cascade + DI rinse (WHY: hydrocarbons prevent condensation adhesion; PVD has no in-tank chemical cleaning like electroplating)
3. solvent/IPA final rinse and spot-free hot-air or vapor dry (WHY: water spots = visible stains under the film)

4. optional electroplated Ni (or Cu+Ni) leveling/barrier layer on carbon steel or brass (WHY: PVD films are pinholed and thin — non-stainless substrates rust through; Ni also brightens/levels) — nickel-release limits (EN 1811 / REACH entry 27 class) apply for skin contact [FACT: regulation exists]
5. rack with clean gloves; parts must be electrically contacted to the biased fixture and free to rotate (WHY: bias etch/densification and line-of-sight coverage both require it)

6. in-vacuum steps 2-5 of operation_sequence (pumpdown, outgas, plasma/arc-ion etch, adhesion interlayer) are the actual adhesion-critical 'pretreatment' (WHY: atomically clean, activated surface is what ion plating buys over plain evaporation)

deposit_properties.purity_karat: Au layers: as-charged purity, typically 99.9%+ = 24k color surface (alloy caps tuned to 1N-5N ISO 8654 colors); TiN/ZrN contain NO gold — marketing must say 'gold-tone PVD' unless a real Au cap is present [FACT]
deposit_properties.hardness_HV: evaporated Au: ~60-90 HV (soft) [FACT: published typical]; TiN: ~2000-2400 HV, ZrN similar class [FACT: published typical] — composite stack scratch resistance is set by the nitride, orders beyond any electroplated hard gold (~130-200 HV)
deposit_properties.thickness_per_pass: one batch = full stack: interlayer 5-50 nm + nitride 0.5-3 um + Au cap 0.05-0.3 um; evaporation-only route 0.05-0.2 um Au per run
deposit_properties.color_control: nitride stoichiometry via N2 flow (grey->gold->brown across increasing N2); ZrN for pale gold; final tone locked by Au/Au-alloy cap; verify vs ISO 8654 master plates — color is a closed-loop process parameter, not a bath additive as in electroplating
deposit_properties.ductility_forming_notes: CRITICAL ANSWER TO PLATE-THEN-FORM: NO for the premium stack — TiN/ZrN are ceramics that crack and spall at roughly >1-2% strain [FACT: published behavior of hard ceramic PVD films], and wire-bending a ring imposes several % outer-fiber strain; additionally arc deposition heat (200-450 C) can temper-soften spring steel. Evaporated soft Au alone is ductile but so thin and (without bias) so weakly adhered that forming/drawing scuffs it off. Rule: FORM AND FINISH FIRST, PVD-COAT LAST. This inverts the owner's continuous coated-wire-then-shape concept; that concept belongs to reel-to-reel ELECTROplating with ductile stacks, not to PVD.

electricity (pumps run hours per batch; arc sources kW-class)

implosion of glass bell jars under vacuum [FACT]
hot surfaces / molten metal in sources [FACT]

controls: interlocked covers on all supplies; earth-bonded chamber; lockout for source access
polycarbonate implosion shield around glass jars; use metal chambers when possible
UV-filtering viewport glass; never view arc directly

diy_feasibility.verdict: SPLIT VERDICT. (a) Thermal evaporation of gold: the MOST DIY-feasible vacuum coating route that exists — simpler than sputtering (no magnetron, no RF), and it works on glass houseware — but it yields only soft 0.05-0.2 um flash that is NOT scratch-resistant and needs lacquer or a subsequent electroplated build-up. (b) Arc ion plating TiN + Au (the actual 'scratch-resistant premium watch look' the owner wants): NOT DIY-buildable at credible quality; the realistic small-producer path is FORM steel/stainless rings in-house, then send racked batches to a commercial PVD job shop (toll coating), or buy a used industrial batch coater once volume justifies it.
diy_feasibility.minimum_viable_setup: DIY evap: bell jar or SS pot chamber, 2-stage rotary + diffusion/turbo pump, Pirani + high-vac gauge, W boat + 50-300 A low-voltage supply, rotating fixture, QCM, shutter, implosion shield — low-thousands USD class used [ESTIMATE: market class, medium confidence]. Premium route: none in-house; job-shop batches, plus in-house polishing/racking/QC (loupe, master color plates, tape-test).
diy_feasibility.hard_limits: line-of-sight + batch nature kills the continuous wire feed-through concept for PVD (that concept maps to reel-to-reel electroplating); plate-then-form is impossible with nitride stacks (ceramic cracks on bending) so all shaping must precede coating; deposition temperature vs spring-steel temper; carbon steel rusts through PVD pinholes (use stainless or Ni-barrier); DIY cannot reach arc-grade adhesion/hardness with evaporation alone
